name: Hampshire Controls Corporation
old_description: Established in 1976 and based in Dover, New Hampshire, Hampshire Controls is a leading designer and manufacturer of supremely reliable “Made in the USA” monitoring, logging, and alert status notification systems for demanding applications.
about:
Hampshire Controls Corporation was established in 1976 in Dover, New Hampshire. The company designs and manufactures monitoring, data logging, and alarm notification systems for demanding applications, emphasizing "Made in the USA" reliability.

The product line includes NIST-traceable temperature monitors and alarms (configurable with 2 to 8 channels), cryogenic temperature monitors, multi-probe condition monitors, the T° Sentry ALERT data logging and alarm system, Wi-Fi temperature transmitters, biomedical freezer backup systems (liquid CO2 and liquid nitrogen), LN2 level monitors, laboratory air flow monitors, and remote alarm delay modules. Manufacturing services encompass PCB soldering, cable manufacturing, subsystem interfacing, final electronic assembly, electronic testing, burn-in, and NIST-traceable calibration, all performed at the Dover facility. The firm also provides custom mechanical and electrical engineering, firmware development, and communication protocol implementation (BACnet, Modbus, MQTT, HTTP/HTTPS, etc.).

Hampshire Controls serves blood banks, cryogenic biologic storage facilities, vaccine and genetic research laboratories, biopharma production plants, governmental agencies, hospitals, commercial food processing and storage operations, and industrial manufacturers. It also supplies original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) with high-volume temperature monitoring and alarm systems for clinical, food and beverage, water distribution, plumbing, and industrial markets.

The company differentiates itself through in-house design, manufacturing, and calibration capabilities, allowing it to offer both standard and custom-engineered products with NIST-traceable calibration. Its systems are UL LISTED and built to meet NEMA/IP ratings for harsh environments.

name: Hanley's Foods
old_description: Hanley’s makes premium, natural salad dressings with a taste of Louisiana.
about:
Hanley's Foods is based in Baton Rouge, Louisiana. The company was founded in 2010 by Richard and Kate Hanley, a couple who have been together since high school. The business originated in 2012 when the pair discovered their favorite restaurant-style dressing, Sensation®, was unavailable in stores. After testing recipes at salad parties with family and friends, they launched the winning formula at the Red Stick Farmers Market, where it sold out repeatedly. They later partnered with the LSU AgCenter's Food Incubator to scale production.

The company manufactures premium salad dressings and croutons, producing every bottle from scratch in its Louisiana facility. Hanley's focuses exclusively on these two product lines, using natural, locally sourced ingredients. Its products are now stocked in more than 2,000 retail locations across the United States.

Hanley's serves the retail grocery and foodservice sectors. Its customer base includes national chains such as Walmart, Costco, Whole Foods Market, and Winn-Dixie, as well as regional grocers like Rouses Markets and AG Stores. The company also supplies foodservice operators including Compass Group and Royal Caribbean.

The founders started Hanley's to bring a beloved local dressing to the broader market. The company emphasizes a single-minded commitment to quality, citing certifications such as HACCP, NSF, SQF, and GMP, and a philosophy of using premium, natural ingredients sourced from south Louisiana.

name: Hansen Plastics Corporation
old_description: Hansen Plastics Corporation: Plastic Manufacturers in Illinois & Custom Injection Molding Services
about:
Hansen Plastics Corporation operates from Elgin, Illinois, where it was founded in 1971 by Elmer Hansen. The company transitioned to an Employee Stock Ownership Plan in 1991 and became fully employee-owned by 1998, a structure that remains central to its culture and decision-making.

The shop runs more than 70 injection molding presses ranging from 28 to 500 tons across over 150,000 square feet of production space. Core processes include horizontal, vertical/insert, and multi-material molding, supported by decoupled molding and RJG scientific molding with cavity-pressure transducers. Value-added operations cover in-mold decorating, hot stamping, pad printing, machining, ultrasonic welding, thermal insertion, assembly, and custom packaging.

Hansen serves OEMs and manufacturers across North America in automotive, life safety, appliances, fluid movement and water treatment, transportation (non-automotive), construction, and agriculture. Long-term customers include Elkay in water delivery and Motive Products in automotive tools.

The company traces its differentiation to its employee-owner model and a founding motto of "do it right the first time." Its quality system is built on ISO 9001:2015 with statistical process control looped into business systems, aiming for zero defects through data-driven process control and lean manufacturing practices.

name: Happy's Gifts and Apparel
old_description: Elevate your Mercer County business with professional custom embroidery from Happy's Gifts and Apparel in Hazen, ND. Perfect for logos on polos, hats, jackets, aprons, and team uniforms. Ideal for oil field crews, schools, churches, farms, and events in Beulah, Hazen, and Stanton.
about:
Happy's Gifts and Apparel operates from a home-based shop in Hazen, North Dakota, serving Mercer County and surrounding communities. The business was started about five years ago by Keith and Morgan, a husband-and-wife team who run the operation as a Christian, family-owned enterprise. Keith, a paramedic of over ten years, began with a miter saw crafting custom woodworking pieces for local customers; demand grew after they added a laser engraver and later an embroidery machine, turning a side project into a full-time custom shop.

The company provides custom embroidery, laser engraving and cutting, screen-printed and embroidered apparel (t‑shirts, polos, hats, hoodies), laser‑engraved stainless‑steel tumblers, and a range of promotional products such as keychains, coozies, trays, awards and magnets. All work is done in‑house with low minimum orders and wholesale pricing for volumes typically ranging from 10 to 100+ pieces. Free design proofs are offered on every project.

Primary customers include oil‑field crews, schools, churches, farms and local businesses in Beulah, Hazen, Stanton and Washburn. The shop also serves event organizers needing tradeshow giveaways, employee‑recognition awards and client‑appreciation gifts, as well as families seeking personalized keepsakes.

Happy's emphasizes local, personal service: customers work directly with the makers, receive free design assistance, and can pick up orders in Hazen to avoid shipping delays. The owners highlight durable stitching and engraving built for North Dakota conditions, competitive wholesale rates, and the convenience of a single source for apparel, drinkware, awards and promotional items.

Harrell's Metal Works, Inc., a family-owned business, was founded in 1985 in Grenada, Mississippi, by Randy Harrell. Over the years, the business grew from ornamental iron work into a significant structural steel fabricator.

It produces fabricated structural steel for a range of projects, leveraging a team of dedicated employees under the leadership of Randy Harrell as owner and president, joined by his son Hunter Harrell as vice president and daughter Haley Harrell Moak.

The company serves contractors and project owners in the ornamental iron, miscellaneous metal, and structural steel sectors, providing subcontracted fabrication services for commercial and industrial construction projects.

Harrell's Metal Works emphasizes consistent, reliable, and cost-effective service, aiming to deliver the highest-quality fabricated structural steel that meets or exceeds project expectations.

name: Haven Steel Products Inc
old_description: Haven Steel Products began construction of its production facility in 1968 and has been a privately-owned company producing spring steel components since 1969. Our company fabricates, and heat treats components for the agricultural industry (tillage components), the construction industry (landscaping and mowing components), the trailer industry (leaf springs), and many other clients.
about:
Haven Steel Products began building its first production facility in Haven, Kansas, in 1968 and started producing spring steel components the following year. The privately owned company was founded as a fabricator for the agricultural, construction, and trailer industries, and the original 7,000‑square‑foot building has since grown to more than 200,000 square feet of production space across two plants in Haven, Kansas, and McKenzie, Tennessee.

The company forges, hot‑forms, heat‑treats, powder‑coats, laser‑cuts, and builds tooling in‑house. Its Kansas plant runs eight quench‑and‑temper lines, a 30 kW Bodor fiber laser with bevel capability on carbon steel up to 2 inches thick, and a new Flex CNC cell; the Tennessee plant recently added two 700‑ton forging presses, a 36‑inch belt furnace, and a slurry‑coating line for Ultra Tuf Coatings™. Together the sites operate multiple natural‑gas furnaces, induction heaters, and a growing fleet of Kuka robots.

Haven Steel supplies heat‑treated and tempered components to major OEMs and short‑line manufacturers in agriculture (tillage sweeps, disc blades, rotary cutter blades), construction (landscaping and mowing parts), trailer production (leaf springs, seat springs, weight‑equalizing hitch springs), railroad (wear plates), recycling (chopper knives), grounds maintenance (aerator knives), playground equipment, and patio furniture.

The company emphasizes full traceability—every shipped part can be traced back to its raw‑steel heat and process history—and maintains an ISO 9001:2015 quality system with third‑party calibrated inspection equipment and a minimum three‑year documentation retention. Recent investments in automation, additional furnace capacity, and the proprietary Ultra Tuf Coatings™ line reflect a focus on extending component wear life three to five times over standard parts.

The shop runs 25 horizontal injection molding machines with clamping forces from 22 to 1,375 tons, supported by an on-site tool room that handles mold construction, repair, and modification. This vertical integration allows the company to manage tooling lead times and respond to design changes without relying on external vendors.

Hawkeye Molding serves a range of sectors including appliance, agricultural equipment, lighting, industrial machinery, office and home furnishings, and furniture. The company also collaborates with a network of mold-building partners in the Midwest and China to supplement capacity or specialized tooling needs.

The company emphasizes responsiveness, integrity, and a Midwestern work ethic as its differentiators, aiming to be a dependable, innovative partner that helps customers succeed through quality, value, and service.
